title: Alert activation journal and shift handbook integration prototype
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description:
Problem: On-call engineers lose context when alerts fire across shifts: multiple consoles, SLA deltas, and cost signals are scattered between Alert detail, SLO dashboards, and the postmortem doc. This ticket explores an in-situ "activation journal" embedded in the shift handbook: a compact timeline that surfaces alert activations, the SLO delta at activation, first-responder notes, quick links to relevant dashboards and postmortem templates, and an inline cost-sensitivity indicator.

Goals: 1) Reduce cognitive switching for responders by collocating the activation timeline + handoff checklist. 2) Reduce time-to-first-action by surfacing jump-to links (live trace, model logs, incident runbook). 3) Surface immediate cost impact estimations (low/medium/high) tied to the activated route/model so responders can triage cost-related regressions. 4) Provide a clear path for creating a postmortem link or tagging an activation to an incident once the handoff is accepted.

Non-goals: This is not a replacement for full incident timelines or long-form postmortems. It does not attempt to perform automated root cause analysis. The cost-sensitivity indicator is intentionally conservative (heuristic-based) for phase 1.
acceptance_criteria: Design mockups include a persistent shift handbook panel with an embedded activation journal timeline

Each activation entry shows timestamp, alert rule name, SLO delta (absolute and %), suggested severity, cost-sensitivity (low/medium/high), and two contextual actions: 'Open live view' and 'Create postmortem link'
Prototype demonstrates a compact handoff flow where an outgoing on-call can attach notes and flag unresolved activations for the incoming rotation
Prototype contains a small 'cost slider' simulation that demonstrates how different batching/quantization recommendations change the cost-sensitivity label
Design review feedback from at least PM, Eng lead (runtime), and SRE incorporated into next iteration
Accessibility checks for timeline keyboard navigation and contrast pass (WCAG AA) documented
tasks: Sketch low-fidelity wireframes for two density modes (compact / expanded)
Create hi-fidelity Figma screens for activation entry, cost-sensitivity microcopy, and handoff acceptance modal
Build clickable Figma prototype linking alert detail -> live view -> postmortem flow
Run 3 x 30-min guerrilla usability sessions with SREs / on-call engineers
Consolidate feedback, write design handoff for ENG grooming session
Add localization notes and accessibility checklist
feedback: PM - Priya Kaur: Love the idea of surfacing SLO delta inline; want a clearer mapping between 'suggested severity' and our existing incident severity taxonomy
Eng Lead - Mateo Alvarez: Engineering worried about the cardinality of linked live views; recommend limiting quick-links to three curated endpoints and adding a 'more...' affordance
SRE - Jordan Lee: Suggests that cost-sensitivity should be derived from recent per-token cost trends and not just model family; flagged as ENG dependency
Design Lead - Elena Rossi: Recommend tone down micro-animations for compact mode to avoid distraction during incident peak; prioritize keyboard navigation
notes: Decision: start with read-only activation journal for phase 1; create-postmortem flow will open the standard incident builder (separate ticket)
Tradeoff: showing too many quick links increases surface area for backend calls — agreed to cache link metadata and lazy-load live views
Accessibility: timeline items must be reachable with up/down arrows and Enter to expand; screen-reader friendly labels required
Next step: ENG grooming on 2026-03-15 to scope backend telemetry and link metadata contract
